concepts.definition: The three parts of a good game: what is to be done, what is at stake and how it will end.
concepts.example: In the fruit hunt, the goal is 8 fruits, the risk is bombs and time, and the ending is winning or losing.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting the risk; if it is impossible to lose, the game has no excitement.

concepts.definition: Dividing the game into small events that each do one job: setup, dropping, collisions, endings.
concepts.example: The bomb penalty is only in the Enemy collision; the winning check is only in the fruit collision.
concepts.pitfall: Piling everything into one event; when there is a bug, it is hard to find where it is.

concepts.term: Countdown and when time runs out
concepts.definition: "start countdown from [n] seconds" starts the time; when the time reaches 0, the "when time runs out" event runs.
concepts.example: When the game starts, start the countdown from 45 seconds.
concepts.pitfall: Leaving the countdown block outside an event; it never runs.

concepts.definition: Inside the fruit collision you write "if score ≥ target, end game: you win".
concepts.example: If score ≥ 8, write "You win!", play the victory melody and end the game.
concepts.pitfall: Using =; if the score jumps over the target, the game cannot be won.

concepts.definition: The game being neither too easy nor impossible; the time, lives, target and speed numbers fitting together.
concepts.example: For 8 fruits in 45 seconds, you need to catch a fruit every 5.6 seconds on average.
concepts.pitfall: Setting the numbers without ever trying them; the game either ends at once or never ends.

quiz.prompt: In the game you need to collect 8 fruits. You catch a fruit every 4 seconds on average. How many seconds do 8 fruits take? (The time is 45 seconds.)
quiz.explanation: 8 × 4 = 32 seconds. That is less than 45 seconds, so at this rate you win before the time runs out (with 13 seconds to spare).

quiz.prompt:
The player catches the 8th fruit at the 30th second. What happens?

```
when game starts:
  start countdown from 45 seconds
when time runs out:
  end game: you lose
when a Player hits a Food:
  change score by 1
  if score ≥ 8:
    end game: you win
```
options: The game is won and ends at once
The game lasts until the 45th second, then it is lost
quiz.explanation: When the score reaches 8, "if" answers yes and "end game: you win" runs. Once the game has ended, the when time runs out event no longer runs.

quiz.prompt:
The time never appears on the screen and the game is never lost when the time runs out. Which is the bug?

```
when game starts:
  set score to 0
  set lives to 5
when time runs out:
  start countdown from 45 seconds
  end game: you lose
```
options: The block that starts the countdown is inside "when time runs out"; it should be put inside "when game starts"
The score has not been reset
"end game" is in the wrong place
quiz.explanation: "when time runs out" only runs if the countdown has started. The countdown never starts, so the time does not appear either. The start block goes in the event that runs at the start of the game.

quiz.prompt: In the fruit hunt, what is the "risk"?
options: The basket going left and right
quiz.explanation: The goal is collecting 8 fruits. The risk is the things the player can lose: lives with the bombs, time with the countdown. The melody is feedback.

quiz.prompt: Inside which event is it best to put the winning check ("if score ≥ 8")?
options: In the fruit collision event, because that is where the score changes
In the when lives run out event
In no event, on its own in the work area
quiz.explanation: The score changes when a fruit is caught, and the check should be made at exactly that moment. The score does not change in the bomb collision; a block standing on its own is not run by any event.
